per step and per layer: one new self-attention row; the
The KV cache. A decoder layer’s self-attention keys and values for past tokens never change — a past token
cannot see the future, so its
are final the moment it is computed. The cache keeps them: each step
computes ONE new row and appends it. Cross-attention is even simpler: its keys and values come from the
encoder, which does not change at all, so they are computed on the first step and reused. The table is the real
cache of sequence A’s first six steps.

svg.text: v2 · KV cache — one new row per step, the rest read back
v1.5 · no cache — every row recomputed, every step
Head 0 of layer 0’s keys, columns 0, 1, 2 and 127. Row p0 is the same four numbers at every step — a past token’s K never changes, so v2 keeps it and v1.5 rebuilds it.

· sequence A · the first two generation steps
Each decoder layer’s cache dict has a "self" drawer and a "cross" drawer. The same method fills both, and one flag,
, decides which rule applies: self-attention appends a row every step, cross-attention computes the encoder’s keys once and then only reads them.
